text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are presenting with hematuria and right flank pain; let's start by asking: have you experienced any fever or chills alongside these symptoms?

text: 42-year-old Caucasian male. The patient reports experiencing visible blood in his urine accompanied by discomfort in his right flank. He denies any recent trauma to the area. He mentions a series of urinary tract infections over the past few years but has not been on renal dialysis.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Given your history of recurrent urinary tract infections and current right flank pain, have you noticed any passage of small, sand-like stones or colic-type pain that radiates toward your groin?

speaker: Doctor
text: That pain is usually severe and comes in waves, right? Have you had any nausea or vomiting associated with it? Also, to confirm the location and severity, do you mind if I perform a physical exam to check for costovertebral angle tenderness?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant previous medical history except noted recurrent urinary tract infections. No history of renal dialysis or known genetic diseases. Social history: Non-smoker, drinks alcohol socially. Works in an office setting.
